repo_prior_art.cite: none; the catalogue's completed ExactID entry eid_lingam_direction_min_order_v1 concerns cumulant-based LiNGAM direction recovery, not competing BACKSHIFT honest-subset overlap.

published_prior_art.cite: RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift Theorem 1 and KleinsteuberShen2013NUJDUniqueness Theorem 1 give complete-family diagonalizer uniqueness; the adversarial candidate-subset overlap application is a supporting adaptation.

repo_prior_art.cite: none; no active or banked proposal addresses an exact whole-covariance-environment replacement radius for BACKSHIFT.

published_prior_art.cite: RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift Theorem 1 is the all-honest iff criterion, while AkhavanEtAl2019GeometryJD and ShenEtAl2020RJDSEM provide robust-JD procedures rather than a worst-case whole-environment replacement radius with a legal two-explanation BACKSHIFT converse.

RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift Corollary 2(ii) treats fully continuous amplitudes; PerryVonKugelgenScholkopf2022SparseShift and PfisterPeters2022SparseIV concern distinct sparse-heterogeneity models and do not derive the affine-occupancy formula under slot replacement.

Afsari2008JDSensitivity studies local sensitivity for a selected joint-diagonalization problem and AndrewsCheng2013SporadicID general identification-robust inference; neither gives a subset-uniform BACKSHIFT certificate atlas or the stated contraction target.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:sharp-replacement-radius / ass:invariant-noise-interior
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The legal alternative-model construction and quantitative conditioning are conditional on an interior invariant covariance Ω ∈ S++p, rather than the full PSD nuisance class allowed by ordinary BACKSHIFT.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Exact replacement radius on the stated interior-noise class; no unrestricted PSD-boundary converse is claimed.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: def:subset-consensus / oeq:certified-uniform-inference
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Finite subset enumeration is only an oracle reduction and assumes full solution sets from a feasibility oracle; it is not a supplied terminating implementation.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Definition-level coverage propagation is settled conditionally on the regions, while certified computability, chart switching, and the uniform modulus remain the open-ended target.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines the invariant-noise/diagonal-shift covariance-difference model and cycle-product-normalized diagonalizer class, proves an all-honest pairwise criterion for unique recovery, and gives an almost-sure continuous-amplitude corollary.

source_verification_receipts.version: Author version corresponding to IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing 61(7), 2013; theorem text inspected in the author version
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper characterizes essential exact non-unitary joint-diagonalizer uniqueness for a supplied diagonal family through a profile-collinearity measure.
The paper retains target matrices using a residual-distance threshold in an iterative joint-diagonalization procedure; it does not state a necessary-and-sufficient adversarial replacement radius.

source_verification_receipts.version: IEEE Transactions on Signal and Information Processing over Networks 6, 2020 publication PDF
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: R-JDSEM uses an elementwise robust joint-diagonalization formulation for sparse within-matrix outliers; its noiseless uniqueness result uses Kruskal-rank and prior-edge information rather than whole covariance-slab replacement.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 4, Corollary 4.2; p. 6, Theorem 5.3 and Corollary 5.4
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves bivariate and high-probability multivariate graph-identification results under probabilistically sparse mechanism shifts, not BACKSHIFT affine occupancy or adversarial covariance-slot replacement.
The paper proves identifiability of sparse causal coefficients in an instrumental-variable model under its rank and support conditions, distinct from sparse BACKSHIFT intervention-support geometry.

source_verification_receipts.version: SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 43(2), 2022
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives congruence-diagonalizability conditions and a numerical procedure for one Hermitian matrix collection, not a complete corrupted-BACKSHIFT subset solver.

source_verification_receipts.version: SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 30(3), 2008
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies nonorthogonal joint-diagonalization uniqueness and local sensitivity as functions of diagonalizer conditioning and a uniqueness modulus.

The paper studies estimation, tests, and confidence sets under sporadic identification failure in smooth sample-average criterion models, not algebraic certificates for corrupted BACKSHIFT covariance families.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a worked all-active sparse-support design at m=2c+3, compute every pairwise incidence count and Mgen, and state it as the explicit attainability corollary for the environment lower bound.
Separate the PSD-noise sufficiency direction from the SPD-only converse in the theorem presentation and identify the PSD-boundary converse as a concrete extension problem.

Turn the certificate handle into an explicit semialgebraic decision procedure with input encoding, termination argument, and complexity bound; this would strengthen the inference agenda into an algorithmic-identifiability contribution.

recommended_next_step: Advance the conditional field-tier radius theorem and generic sparse-support frontier to Stage 0; retain the certificate and uniform-inference program as the stated open target.
